after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to  $\operatorname{tanh}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡y)?$
after.worked_solution:
The definition of $\operatorname{tanh}⁡x$ is 
        

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x & =\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}-1}{{e}^{2x}+1} \\  & =\frac{1-{e}^{-2x}}{1+{e}^{-2x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the second definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{{e}^{2(3\operatorname{ln}⁡y)}-1}{{e}^{2(3\operatorname{ln}⁡y)}+1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{6\operatorname{ln}⁡y}-1}{{e}^{6\operatorname{ln}⁡y}+1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡{y}^{6}}-1}{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡{y}^{6}}+1} \\  & =\frac{{y}^{6}-1}{{y}^{6}+1}.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x & =\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}-1}{{e}^{2x}+1} \\  & =\frac{1-{e}^{-2x}}{1+{e}^{-2x}}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Question 4

Which of the following is equivalent to tanh⁡(1t), for t≠0?

a
e2/t−1e2/t+1
b
2e1/t−12e1/t+1
c
e2t−1e2t+1
d
e2/t+1e2/t−1
e
e2t+1e2t−1
Submit

decision.explanation: Using tanh(x)=(e^{2x}-1)/(e^{2x}+1) and substituting x=1/t gives (e^{2/t}-1)/(e^{2/t}+1), which is option a.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to  $\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\frac{1}{t}),$ for $t\ne 0?$
after.worked_solution:
The definition of $\operatorname{tanh}⁡x$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x & =\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}-1}{{e}^{2x}+1} \\  & =\frac{1-{e}^{-2x}}{1+{e}^{-2x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the second definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\frac{1}{t}) & =\frac{{e}^{2(1/t)}-1}{{e}^{2(1/t)}+1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2/t}-1}{{e}^{2/t}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$
